title: The Clock
paragraphs: A mystery and suspense anthology introduced by the personified Clock, presenting compact stories of crime, irony, danger, and unexpected consequences.
U.S. ABC suspense anthology created by Lawrence Klee and framed by the personified Clock/Father Time.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: ABC New York production (November 3, 1946 to February 26, 1948) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] and ABC Hollywood production (March 4, 1948 to May 23, 1948) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Charles Webster (performer), Clark Andrews (director), Gene Kirby (announcer), Lawrence Klee (writer and creator), Bernard Green (composer, music director, and performer), Basil Adlam (conductor and music director), and Joe DeSantis (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].

The stories often return to time, fate and consequences, deception, hidden identity and manipulation, love, jealousy and relationship conflict, crime and wrongdoing, supernatural or uncanny threat, and money, greed and financial motive.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar suspense anthology boom, New York-to-Hollywood production migration, Sustaining network economics and cancellation, and Separate Australian adaptation.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|suspense|Suspense]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]], and [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]].
